newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close slightly down in caution.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close slightly down in caution.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended slightly lower on Tuesday as persistent profit-taking in blue-chip electronic shares dampened overall sentiment, brokers said.
The weighted index ended 10.03 points or 0.15 percent lower at 6,616.38.
Turnover was a modest T$42.74 billion.

Electronics -- which had boosted the index recently on sound profit expectations and news that the U.S. semiconductor book-to-bill ratio hit a new year high in September -- eased by 0.15 percent on continued mild profit-taking.
"The market failed to find another strong sector to hold itself up after investors started selling electronic shares," said Joe Chiou of Taiwan Securities Investment.

Winbond lost 3.9 percent or T$1.20 to T$29.60 after a fire on Monday damaged its unfinished wafer plant. Shamrock Technology, which debuted on the stock market on Friday, saw its honeymoon end by falling 3.59 percent or T$1.60 to T$43.

Textiles outperformed the market, slipping a negligible 0.01 percent. "The sector is expected to perform well in the fourth quarter, which is typically the best season for exports," said Michael Hung of Nikko Securities.
Brokers said Wall Street's rise to another record high overnight failed to excite the domestic market.

However, electronics shares could soon shrug off the current selling mood as most companies in the sector are expected to report sound earnings for the first three quarters of 1996 in the imminent reporting period, brokers said.
The deadline for firms to report January-September earning totals is October 31.
A range of 6,600-6,650 was seen for Wednesday.
